Mastering Bash Scripting for Automated Backups

May 28, 2026 6 min read

Automation is the cornerstone of efficient system administration. Writing Bash scripts is the easiest way to orchestrate tasks, but writing reliable scripts requires structured error boundaries.

1. Use Exit-on-Error Flags

Start your script with sensible flags to ensure it halts immediately when a command fails:

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
  • -e: Exit immediately if a command exits with a non-zero status.
  • -u: Treat unset variables as an error.
  • -o pipefail: The return value of a pipeline is the status of the last command to exit with a non-zero status.

2. Safe Backup Routines

Ensure backup directories exist and handle permission restrictions gracefully. Compress assets using tar with timestamp files for easy retrieval.
